newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. military needed for Panama anti-drug center.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military needed for Panama anti-drug center.

text.p: The commander of U.S. forces in Latin America said on Friday a possible international anti-drug centre on Howard Air Force Base in Panama would require a U.S. military presence of at least 2,000 to be operational.
"Howard Air Force Base today ... runs about 8,000 counter-drug flights a year. It takes about 2,000 airmen to keep that base in operation," SOUTHCOM head Gen. Wesley Clark told Reuters.
The United States and Panama have been holding preliminary talks to turn Howard, located at the Pacific entrance to the Panama Canal, into an international anti-drugs centre.

"We're going to have to look at what's required," Clark said in an interview at his Panama City office. "That's a matter to be worked out in the discussions and negotiations with the government of Panama."
Clark, whom President Bill Clinton has nominated as commander of all allied NATO forces and American troops in Europe, said a final decision could come this year.
"We're approaching very rapidly the time to make a decision," he said. "We would certainly hope this year."

The planned centre would not "be a multinational institution, which has multinational forces which go out and take action", he said, but all of its actions "as we envision it would be taken by sovereign national forces."

Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares had said his government would not negotiate with the United States a military presence in Panama in the next century. But he said the United States could keep Howard at no cost for use as an anti-drug centre.
The United States is to turn over control of the Panama Canal and withdraw all troops and bases by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral canal treaties.
